constraints.rationale: Both carry the advertised-route validation rule: isSameOriginRelativeHref is a boolean wrapper that builds a synthetic ready POST capability and calls resolveAdvertisedRoute, so the href checks it answers for the panels' usable gates are defined entirely in resolveAdvertisedRoute's same-origin, no-credentials, no-fragment rules.

queryGraph is the graph half of one fusion POST workflow split across two files: it delegates the request, error-envelope handling and FusionResponse parsing to postFusionRequest with want: ["graph"] and the "Graph query" label that postFusionRequest's signature enumerates. Reading queryGraph's invalid-response check without postFusionRequest's parse and error paths gives only half the contract.

BootstrapDependencies is the dependency contract and the page's bootstrap constant is its only implementation: the page supplies the three loaders and the five callbacks that write capabilities, inventory, projectSummary, loading and error. Changing a callback's meaning on either side requires the other.

They are the two halves of the D4 self-healing poll: isFullyReady's doc comment defines when the workbench needs no further poll, and createReadinessPoller's sync(notReady) is driven by exactly !isFullyReady(capabilities) in the page. The poller's start/stop semantics only make sense alongside the verdict that feeds it.

The shell's coverage derived value is deriveReadinessCoverage applied to the capability readiness signals, and both carry the same D4 comment about not trusting the backend's overall field. The Overall readiness banner's ready/partial verdict and its "Covers ..." list are the covered and building arrays this function computes.

loadCapabilities is the only producer of the incompatible_version error kind (it rewraps CapabilityContractError), the page's onError forwards that kind, and the shell's incompatible flag is the only consumer, switching the heading to "Incompatible workbench contract" and hiding the retry button (WorkbenchShell.svelte:131-142). The failure and its presentation are one responsibility across three files.

resourceError translates a WorkbenchClientError's kind, retryable and message fields one-to-one into the ResourceState error branch that the shell renders, including whether a Retry button appears. Whoever changes the error's retryable rule for 5xx in fetchJSON needs resourceError's mapping in view and vice versa.

resultQuery is kept separate from the live input precisely so it can drive queried-symbol selection, and it is passed to GraphView as queriedName, where groups = groupEntities(graph.nodes, queriedName) implements the D6 rule (queried symbol first and selected, unresolved endpoints grouped below). The same groupEntities call with resultQuery picks the panel's default selectedHandle at GraphPanel.svelte:130-133.

The page binds onRetry={refresh}, so every Retry button in the shell (connection, inventory at line 237, project summary at lines 304-306) runs the page's refresh, which clears the error, re-raises loading when there are no capabilities yet and re-runs the bootstrap. The retry affordance and the retry behaviour are one workflow split across the route and the component.

submit's catch branch copies FusionSearchError's message, code and retryable into the panel's error state, and the markup shows the code and offers Retry search only when retryable is true. The error class's fields exist for this consumer; a non-FusionSearchError gets the generic non-retryable fallback.

Same name and nearly the same $derived gate (availability ready, method POST, isSameOriginRelativeHref), so a shallow reader sees one symbol. They gate different capabilities fed from different keys (queries.code_search vs queries.graph_projection) and the graph gate adds the fusion_graph_projection contract check; grouping them merges the code-search panel with the graph drill-down.

Both present an "index is <state>" string with underscores turned into spaces, so the shared term "index state" makes them look like one presentation concern. queryNotice reports the per-response index field of a single graph query and tells the user existing graph state was retained; indexStateLabel labels the capability document's structural/semantic readiness signals in the Authoritative state section, with the D3 reset_required special case. One is transient query feedback, the other is workbench readiness.

Identical name and the same three-line idiom (bump generation, abort the controller, null it), which is pure stale-request scaffolding. The bootstrap cancel ends the capabilities/inventory/summary load on page teardown; the GraphPanel cancel aborts an in-flight graph query from the Cancel button at GraphPanel.svelte:225. Different lifecycles, different requests.

Both are "selected*" state that opens a detail pane beside a list of results, the same master-detail shape. selectedNode resolves a bindable graph handle to a CanonicalGraphNode for the entity navigator's facts and relationships; selectedIndex is a position into a code-search FusionResponse.nodes array that is reset on every search. Graph entity selection and search-result selection are different subjects.

Two Error subclasses with the same constructor shape (message, kind-or-code, retryable, optional status) and the same disconnected/invalid_payload vocabulary. WorkbenchClientError is thrown by fetchJSON and loadCapabilities for the GET bootstrap resources and consumed by resourceError and the page's onError; FusionSearchError is thrown by postFusionRequest for fusion POST queries and consumed by the two panels. Neither file imports the other.

Both are ReturnType<typeof setInterval> | null handles with the same clearInterval-then-null teardown, so the setInterval boilerplate makes them look like one timer concern. The poller's timer re-runs the whole bootstrap every 10 s while readiness is not ready (D4 self-healing); elapsedTimer increments a seconds counter for the Searching... status line and is stopped per request.

Same prop name and Capability type, and both branch on availability to show Not ready or Unsupported. CapabilityCard is a passive badge for project_views and the okf_export action, never touching the href; GraphPanel's capability is the graph_projection query route whose href is validated and POSTed to. A capability advertisement card and a query endpoint are different responsibilities.

Both map the literal "not_ready" to "Not ready", so the overloaded status term makes them look like one labelling helper. stateLabel labels ResourceState.status of the inventory and project-summary loads (loading/ready/empty/not_ready/unsupported/error) in the resource sections; badge labels Capability.availability (ready/not_ready/unsupported) of an advertised action card. Resource load state and capability advertisement are different vocabularies.

Both are small *Location formatters that turn a record's path into a display string. nodeLocation renders a FusionNode's path:start-end for a code-search result; sourceLocation picks a ManifestSource's path, paths, url or urls for the configured-sources inventory list. Search results and source inventory are separate subjects that only share the word location.

Two loaders with an identical scaffold (advertisedState, resolveAdvertisedRoute GET, fetchJSON, namespace check, empty-or-ready, resourceError), which is what makes them look like one function. They load different resources from different capability keys (source_inventory vs project_summary) through different contract parsers, apply different empty rules, and feed separate shell sections (Sources vs Project summary) with their own derived values and retry buttons.
